claim:
Let \(P=A_1\oplus\cdots\oplus A_h\) and \(Q=B_1\oplus\cdots\oplus B_k\) be nonempty finite weak-order \(T_0\)-spaces, with \(|A_i|=r_i\ge1\) and \(|B_j|=q_j\ge1\). Put \(Q_0=0\) and \(Q_j=\sum_{t=1}^j q_t\). For \(r\ge1\) and \(x\ge0\), define
\[
a_j(r,x)=q_j\big((x+1)^r-x^r\big),\qquad
b_j(r,x)=(x+q_j)^r-x^r-a_j(r,x).
\]
Define two state counts \(S_j^{(i)}\) and \(M_j^{(i)}\): among order-preserving maps from the first \(i\) source levels, \(S_j^{(i)}\) counts those whose \(i\)-th source level has maximum occupied target level \(j\) and occupies exactly one point of \(B_j\), while \(M_j^{(i)}\) counts those occupying at least two points of \(B_j\). Initialize
\[
S_j^{(1)}=a_j(r_1,Q_{j-1}),\qquad M_j^{(1)}=b_j(r_1,Q_{j-1}).
\]
For \(i\ge2\) and \(1\le j\le k\), write \(x_{u,j}=Q_{j-1}-Q_u\) for \(u<j\). Then
\[
S_j^{(i)}=S_j^{(i-1)}+\sum_{u<j}\left(M_u^{(i-1)}a_j(r_i,x_{u,j})+S_u^{(i-1)}a_j(r_i,x_{u,j}+1)\right),
\]
\[
M_j^{(i)}=\sum_{u<j}\left(M_u^{(i-1)}b_j(r_i,x_{u,j})+S_u^{(i-1)}b_j(r_i,x_{u,j}+1)\right).
\]
Consequently,
\[
|\operatorname{Map}(P,Q)|=\sum_{j=1}^k\left(S_j^{(h)}+M_j^{(h)}\right).
\]
Thus the exact number of continuous maps between arbitrary finite weak orders is computed by \(2k\) transfer states and \(O(hk^2)\) integer-arithmetic transitions.

correctness.rationale: For an order-preserving prefix map, every earlier source level maps below every image point of the immediately preceding source level. In a weak-order target, the common-upper-bound set of that preceding image is determined exactly by its maximum occupied target level and whether its top-level image is a singleton: a singleton contributes its unique point plus all higher levels, while a multiple top-level image permits only higher levels. The functions counted by a_j and b_j are respectively the maps using exactly one or at least two distinct points at the new maximum target level, so initialization, carry, and all u<j transitions are disjoint and exhaustive. The packaged independent brute-force enumerator agrees with the recurrence for all 225 ordered pairs of level compositions of total size at most four and for four larger anchors, but the proof, not the enumeration, establishes the unbounded theorem.

Pouzet–Zaguia, DOI 10.1016/j.disc.2006.05.038, gives weak-order structure and endomorphism lemmas for perpendicular orders but no broader map-enumeration theorem that specializes to the displayed recurrence.

originality.rationale: Exact alias searches and primary-source inspection found the finite-space/order correspondence and structural results on weak-order endomorphisms, but no formula for the number of all maps between arbitrary weak orders and no equivalent two-state transfer recurrence. The closest indexed weak-order result concerns interval-endomorphism algebra dimensions, a different invariant. Previously established exact counts for height-two spaces and specific minimal-sphere-model pairs are strict special cases and do not imply the arbitrary-level recurrence.

value.rationale: The cardinality of a finite mapping space is a natural invariant and a necessary baseline for subsequent study of its specialization order, components, and core. The result compresses all extension information to two states per target level and computes every source/target weak-order pair in O(hk^2) transfer operations, including singleton and nonuniform levels. It unifies previously isolated exact counts such as 44 and 738 while producing arbitrary new instances without brute-force enumeration; this is a structural recurrence rather than a one-off table recomputation.
